text: Chorote is a Matacoan language of South America, spoken by around 2000 people in Argentina, Bolivia and Paraguay. The language's two dialects, Iyojwa'ja and Iyo'wujwa, are fairly distinct from each other and some linguists consider them separate languages.

text: Iyo’wujwa Chorote is a stable indigenous language of Argentina and Paraguay. It belongs to the Matacoan language family. The language is used as a first language by all in the ethnic community. It is not known to be taught in schools.
